description: Eclipse BaSyx is open-source Industry 4.0 middleware and one of the first implementations of digital twins based on the Asset Administration Shell (AAS), the standard digital twin interface for manufacturing assets. It supports type 1, 2 and 3 shells for static data, live data and active negotiation, exchanges live data between physical systems and their twins over OPC UA and MQTT for real-time monitoring and control, and offers basic manufacturing execution functions for service-oriented production. The platform provides ready-to-use components delivered as Docker containers, deployable from a single server to a data centre, and software development kits for Java, C++ and C#; the IDTA Submodel Template Repository is built on it. The project was funded by the German Federal Ministry for Education and Research through the BaSys 4.0, BaSys4.2, uberProd and BaSys4Transfer projects, with a monthly open community hour. Use is international through the Eclipse community. The site footer lists the Eclipse Public License. Caveats: building a twin requires AAS modelling and integration work. For simulation it is the data backbone for manufacturing digital twins that link plant equipment to models and analytics. Related catalogue records include the NIST smart manufacturing test bed data and Siemens Plant Simulation.
